newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Primac to take court action on bid.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Primac to take court action on bid.

text.p: Primac Holdings Ltd said on Friday it would apply to the Supreme Court of Queensland on Monday to restrain dispatch of a formal takeover document from unwelcome takeover suitor IAMA Ltd.

Primac managing director Steve Morrow said the Primac board considered the Part A takeover document from the fellow rural services group was defective and that did not comply with Corporation Law disclosure requirements.
"We are required to take this action because in our opinion, the Corporations Law requirements for adequate disclosure have not been met," Morrow said in a statement.
Primac directors earlier rejected IAMA's 9-for-10 share offer which they said valued Primac at well below current market prices.
"It is well over a month since IAMA announced their offer," Morrow said. "They have had plenty of time to provide adequate forecasts and other information for Primac shareholders."
The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) said earlier this month it would not oppose the planned acquisition of Primac by IAMA.
The ACCC found the rural merchandise market in which both companies operated appeared to be competitive in relevant markets in Queensland and northern New South Wales.
Primac shares closed unchanged at A$2.89 on Friday while IAMA shares closed two cents higher at A$2.87.
At current prices, Primac is valued at A$198 million.
